entry.title: Ascendium Grant on Condensed Courses
entry.content: We received a three-year grant from the Ascendium Education Group. In collaboration with researchers and practitioners across UC Irvine and Virginia Community Colleges, we will conduct research to understand the role and improvement strategies for condensed courses at community colleges.

entry.title: GIAS Research Awards
entry.content: Dr. Yu received a Transformative Research Award from the Edmund W. Gordon Institute for Advanced Study to support a new project on online communication inequalities in the age of AI, and PhD student Zhen Xu is named a W.E.B. Du Bois Scholar to work on the project. Congratulations!

entry.title: Unizin Grant on Teaching and Learning Experience in the Age of AI

link.title: Unizin Grant on Teaching and Learning Experience in the Age of AI

entry.content: We received a one-year grant from the Unizin Consortium. In collaboration with researchers at University of Wisconsin and University of Nebraska, we will track teaching and learning experience across three institutions in the age of AI.
entry.summary: We received a one-year grant from the Unizin Consortium. In collaboration with researchers at University of Wisconsin and University of Nebraska, we will track teaching and learning experience across three institutions in the age of AI.

entry.title: Research on Student Writing in the Age of AI Covered by the Hechinger Report

entry.content: New working paper on changes in student writing after generative AI became available was covered by the Hechinger Report, an influential non-profit newsroom covering inequality and innovation in education.

entry.title: John Castellan Student Paper Award
entry.content: Congratulations to first-year PhD student Zhen Xu for receiving the John Castellan Student Paper Award from the Society for Computation in Psychology! This annual award honors the most outstanding student paper on the application of computational or computerized methods to any area of psychology.

entry.title: PEAR Fellowship
entry.content: Congratulations to first-year PhD student Daniel March for receiving the Postsecondary Education Applied Research (PEAR) Fellowship to support his doctoral study! This fellowship provides doctoral students with training in advanced quantitative analysis and the practical skills needed for a career in applied research in postsecondary education.
